IRAN FM ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF PUSHING U.S. INTO WAR Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “serpent,” accusing him of manipulating Washington into joining the war against Iran. Araghchi cited Netanyahu’s Hebrew-language remarks about influencing the U.S. Netanyahu previously said it took him “a long time” to persuade Washington to join Israel in the conflict.

META COULD OVERTAKE GOOGLE SEARCH IN AD REVENUE Meta is on track to surpass Google Search in advertising revenue by the end of 2026, according to Bernstein. Meta captured nearly half of every incremental digital ad dollar in Q2. Bernstein says AI is accelerating ad growth by improving recommendations, targeting, measurement and conversions, with Meta, Google and Amazon among the biggest beneficiaries.

SAUDI ARABIA EXPLORES $8 BILLION LOAN AS WAR STRAINS FINANCES Saudi Arabia is in early talks to raise at least $8 billion in fresh loans as the Iran war pressures its economy and finances. Saudi Aramco is also discussing potential borrowing with banks. The kingdom posted a $9.1 billion Q2 deficit, while its oil sector contracted nearly 25% amid attacks and regional trade disruptions.

BOFA WARNS INFLATION IS SQUEEZING CONSUMER STAPLES Bank of America says rising commodity costs and limited pricing power are increasing margin pressure on consumer staples companies. Oil, diesel and agricultural prices have surged amid geopolitical and trade disruptions, while cocoa jumped 102% in three months. BofA sees Conagra, Campbell’s, Pilgrim’s Pride and General Mills among the companies most exposed to cost inflation.

HORMUZ DISRUPTIONS SEND TANKER RATES TO RECORD HIGHS Tanker freight rates have surged to record levels as restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz squeezes vessel availability, S&P Global Energy says. Ship crossings have fallen more than 80% since the U.S.-Iran war began on Feb. 28. The strait normally handles about 20% of global seaborne oil and LNG flows. The benchmark Middle East Gulf-Japan LR2 tanker rate hit a record $107.72 per metric ton on Aug. 27.

BESSENT HITS BACK AT DRUCKENMILLER OVER BOND CRITICISM Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended his U.S. bond-market intervention after criticism from Stanley Druckenmiller. Bessent suggested the veteran investor “lost money” around the time he submitted his critical op-ed. He also defended Treasury performance, saying U.S. bonds have been the best-performing market since President Trump took office.

FORMER CREDIT SUISSE RISK HEAD SEES BITCOIN AT $150,000 CK Zheng, former Credit Suisse global head of valuation risk, says Bitcoin’s worst may be over and expects it to reach $150,000 by late 2027. Zheng sees regulatory clarity, institutional adoption and potential passage of the CLARITY Act driving the next bull cycle. He also expects rising U.S. debt to increase demand for Bitcoin and gold as dollar-debasement hedges. Bitcoin currently trades near $78,535.

GOLD FALLS 1% AS FED, MIDDLE EAST PRESSURE MOUNTS Gold posted a second straight loss as renewed Middle East military action and hawkish Fed expectations pressured prices. Front-month gold settled 1% lower at $4,431.10/oz, but still gained 9.4% in August. Silver fell 1.2% to $66.221/oz, while posting a 15% monthly gain. Markets now turn to upcoming U.S. inflation and labor data for direction.

TRUMP APPROVAL STUCK AT RECORD-LOW 33% — REUTERS/IPSOS President Trump’s approval rating remains at 33%, the lowest level of his political career, according to Reuters/Ipsos. Dissatisfaction centers on the Iran war and cost of living, with 71% disapproving of Trump’s handling of living costs and only 36% approving of the war. Ahead of November’s midterms, 46% of Democrats say they are very enthusiastic about voting, versus 31% of Republicans. Among independents, 36% favor Democrats for Congress

AAPL - APPLE ALLEGES OPENAI DEFENDANT USED TRADE SECRETS TO TRAIN AI Apple alleges a defendant in its trade-secret case against OpenAI accessed a proprietary power-converter circuit schematic while at OpenAI and used confidential Apple information to train an AI agent, according to a legal filing. Apple says the new evidence came from a MacBook provided by OpenAI on Aug. 21 during legal proceedings. The company is asking a U.S. federal court to expedite discovery in the case.

BESSENT: HORMUZ COULD BE “WORTHLESS” IN TWO YEARS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Strait of Hormuz could lose its strategic importance within two years as new oil pipelines bypass the waterway. Speaking in North Carolina, Bessent predicted alternative pipeline routes would reduce reliance on the key Persian Gulf energy corridor. “In two years, the Strait of Hormuz will be like a worthless piece of water,” he said.

30-YEAR TREASURY YIELD ERASES INTERVENTION DROP The 30-year Treasury yield surged as high as 5.286%, its highest since August 18. That’s near levels seen before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s bond-market intervention last month, which temporarily pushed yields lower. The impact has proved short-lived, with the 30-year yield recently trading just below 5.26%, signaling renewed pressure on long-term U.S. borrowing costs.

YARDENI: U.S. DEBT CRISIS NOT IMMINENT Yardeni Research acknowledges growing U.S. debt risks, with public debt above $40 trillion, annual interest costs exceeding $1 trillion, and the deficit near 6% of GDP. However, it argues a crisis is not yet imminent. Yardeni says the 10-year Treasury yield between 4% and 5% remains consistent with a healthy economy and warns that betting against stocks over debt fears has been costly.

JPMORGAN: RISING YIELDS WON’T KILL STOCK RALLY JPMorgan remains bullish on global equities, arguing higher bond yields largely reflect stronger economic growth rather than worsening inflation. The bank expects solid earnings growth and sees limited risk of aggressive central-bank tightening. JPMorgan favors cyclical stocks and expects market leadership to broaden beyond AI. Within technology, its preference is semiconductors over hyperscalers and higher-risk AI plays.

BANK OF AMERICA VP KILLED IN TIMES SQUARE ATTACK Bank of America Vice President Erin Piacenti was fatally stabbed in Times Square on Monday during an apparently random attack. A 68-year-old tourist was also stabbed and hospitalized in stable condition. Police confronted the knife-wielding suspect, Pamela Cisneros, 49, who was fatally shot after Tasers failed to stop her. NYPD said investigators have no reason to believe the attack was terrorism-related.
